source_row.rationale: Vaccines are sensitive biological products that require maintenance of an unbroken "cold chain" (appropriate temperature range) from manufacture through administration, since exposure to temperatures outside the recommended range (too warm or, for some vaccines, freezing) can reduce potency and effectiveness, potentially compromising the vaccine's ability to provide adequate immunity.
source_row.source_detail: Storage principles: recommended temperatures must be maintained from receipt through use because excursions can reduce/destroy potency; updated 2024-06-18; accessed 2026-08-14.
source_row.source_name: CDC — Storage and Handling of Immunobiologics
source_row.stem: A nurse is responsible for maintaining proper vaccine storage in a clinic refrigerator, and a new hire assumes the temperature really only matters during shipping from the manufacturer, not once it's sitting in the clinic.
